name: Augustinus Hipponensis
pdTranslations: Extensive NPNF (Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers) coverage including Confessions, doctrinal treatises, anti-heretical works, letters, and selected sermons. Many individual works in 19th-century Library of the Fathers series.
modernTranslations: Ongoing 'The Works of Saint Augustine: A Translation for the 21st Century' project by Augustinian Heritage Institute (multiple volumes published). Fathers of the Church series contains numerous individual works (De Magnitude Animae, De Beata Vita, etc.). Multiple modern scholarly translations of major works.
untranslatedHighlights: Some biblical commentaries remain partially untranslated; enarrationes on specific psalms have selective translation rather than complete coverage.

name: Auctor incertus
pdTranslations: Individual works in this miscellaneous bucket require per-work triage. Unknown which specific works have English translation.
modernTranslations: Unknown; requires inventory of constituent works.
untranslatedHighlights: This is an anonymous/miscellaneous collection that needs disaggregation before translation status can be determined.

name: Rabanus Maurus
pdTranslations: None in ANF/NPNF/Library of the Fathers (post-dates their scope). Helen Waddell, Medieval Latin Lyrics (1929) — selected poems; 'Veni Creator Spiritus' on Wikisource; Peter Wyetzner's Commentary on Esther freely available online.
modernTranslations: Priscilla Throop, De Universo complete in 2 vols (MedievalMS, 2009 — all 22 books of the encyclopedia). Owen M. Phelan, On the Formation of Clergy (De institutione clericorum), FOTC Medieval Continuations, CUA Press 2023 — first English translation. David Mycoff, Life of St. Mary Magdalene (Cistercian CS 108, 1989; attribution uncertain). Commentary on Ruth/Judith/Esther (Scriptorium Press). Roughly 10-15% of corpus translated.
untranslatedHighlights: The bulk of his corpus — massive biblical commentaries (Matthew, Pauline epistles, Kings, Chronicles, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Wisdom, Sirach, Maccabees), De clericorum disciplina, homilies, martyrology — remains Latin-only.

name: Hieronymus Stridonensis
pdTranslations: NPNF Jerome volume (NPNF2-06) contains principal works including biblical prefaces, select commentaries on gospels, prefaces to Vulgate books, and prefaces to commentaries on minor prophets. Library of the Fathers contains selected translations.
modernTranslations: Fathers of the Church series: Commentary on Matthew (FOTC, recent ed.). Additional modern scholarly editions of select commentaries. Some epistles and prefaces translated.
untranslatedHighlights: Majority of Jerome's biblical commentaries remain untranslated into English, particularly extended commentaries on OT books (Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, etc.) and many epistolary works.

name: Rupertus Tuitiensis
pdTranslations: No public-domain translations located.
modernTranslations: Fathers of the Church Medieval Continuations: Commentary on the Songs of Songs (2024, trans. Jieon Kim & Vittorio Hösle). This is the first complete English translation of any Rupert work. Rupert produced 250+ extant manuscripts, but nearly all remain in Latin.
untranslatedHighlights: De divinis officiis (On the Divine Services, most manuscript-rich work), biblical commentaries on multiple OT/NT books, theological treatises on redemption and Eucharist—essentially the entire corpus except Songs of Songs.

name: Auctores varii
pdTranslations: Individual works in this miscellaneous bucket require per-work triage. Unknown which specific works have English translation.
modernTranslations: Unknown; requires inventory of constituent works.
untranslatedHighlights: This is an anonymous/miscellaneous collection of various authors that needs disaggregation before translation status can be determined.

name: Innocentius III
pdTranslations: Selected letters translated in 19th-century scholarly works.
modernTranslations: Catholic University of America Press (FOTC Medieval): The Deeds of Pope Innocent III (first translation into any modern language, trans. James M. Powell). Selected Letters of Pope Innocent III Concerning England (1198–1216) ed. C.R. Cheney & W.H. Semple. Individual letters occasionally translated in academic publications.
untranslatedHighlights: The vast majority of Innocent's papal registers (several thousand letters) remain untranslated. Most of his doctrinal writings, administrative correspondence, and policy letters are only available in Latin.

name: Gregorius I
pdTranslations: The Book of Pastoral Rule (Regulae Pastoralis Liber) in NPNF volume 212. Selected epistles. Some homilies included in NPNF.
modernTranslations: Modern translation of Pastoral Rule by George E. Demacopoulos (Popular Patristics Series, SVS Press)—first new English translation in over 50 years. Individual homilies translated in modern collections and scholarly works. Homiliary collections available.
untranslatedHighlights: Some of Gregory's voluminous letter collection remains incompletely translated. Certain biblical commentaries (Moralia in Job sections) may have gaps in modern English translation.

name: Beda
pdTranslations: The Ecclesiastical History of the English People available in multiple 19th-century English translations (revisions by A.M. Sellar, Giles, Stevens). Various biblical commentaries and homilies translated in NPNF and 19th-c. collections.
modernTranslations: Modern translations of Ecclesiastical History (multiple editions by scholars). Commentaries on Song of Songs and selected writings published by modern presses. Homilies on the Gospels translated. Online Library of Liberty contains 8-volume complete works in English.
untranslatedHighlights: Some of Bede's biblical commentaries on OT books (Genesis, other pentateuchal books) and certain technical scientific/chronological tracts may have partial or incomplete modern translation coverage.

name: Haymo Halberstatensis
pdTranslations: No public-domain English translations located in NPNF, Library of the Fathers, or CCEL.
modernTranslations: No modern English translations located in Fathers of the Church, ACW, TTH series, or other standard medieval translation programs.
untranslatedHighlights: Haymo's extensive biblical commentaries (Psalms, Isaiah, 12 Prophets, Paul's Epistles, Revelation), homilies, and theological treatises all appear to remain in Latin. Works traditionally preserved in PL vols. 116–118 have not been translated.

name: Petrus Lombardus
pdTranslations: None found — no 19th-century or early modern English translations identified.
modernTranslations: Giulio Silano, The Sentences, complete in 4 vols (PIMS Toronto, Mediaeval Sources in Translation 42/43/45/48, 2007–2010) — the only complete English translation of all four books, based on Brady's critical edition. Partial alternatives: Franciscan Archive online Book I; Elizabeth Rogers' portions of Book IV (1917/1976); Psalms-commentary preface in Minnis & Scott, Medieval Literary Theory and Criticism (Oxford, 1988). Roughly 25-30% of PL corpus translated.
untranslatedHighlights: The Magna Glossatura on the Psalms (~1,240 PL columns) and the Collectanea on the Pauline epistles — together the majority of his PL word count — have no English translation (confirmed negative). Sermons untranslated. No FOTC or TTH volumes.

name: Ambrosius Mediolanensis
pdTranslations: NPNF volume 210 contains selected works: Exposition of the Christian Faith, Lectures on the Psalms, Addresses/Sermons (death of Ambrose's brother, emperors Valentinian and Theodosius), Letters. Library of the Fathers contains selected sermons.
modernTranslations: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke (trans. Sr. Ide Ni Riain, Halcyon Press/Elo Publications, 2001). Selected modern editions of individual works. Some homilies in contemporary collections.
untranslatedHighlights: Large portions of Ambrose's extensive biblical commentary corpus (Genesis, other OT books, NT epistles) remain untranslated. Theological treatises (De Officiis, De Bono Mortis) have limited modern English translation. Hymns partially translated.

name: Gerhohus Reicherspergensis
pdTranslations: No public-domain English translations located.
modernTranslations: No dedicated English translations located in Fathers of the Church, ACW, TTH, or Cistercian Publications series.
untranslatedHighlights: Gerhoh's principal work, Expositio in Psalmis (10-part psalms commentary, 1144–1169), remains untranslated. Other works on dogmatic theology, church discipline, canon law, liturgy, and monastic life appear only in Latin (critical edition: van den Eynde & Rijmersdael, 1955–56).

name: Auctor incertus (Augustinus Hipponensis?)
pdTranslations: Cannot determine without specific work identification. If Augustinian, follows Augustine's translation status.
modernTranslations: Cannot determine without specific work identification.
untranslatedHighlights: This is an uncertain-attribution or miscellaneous bucket possibly linked to Augustine. Requires textual identification of constituent works for accurate translation triage.

name: Bernardus Claraevallensis
pdTranslations: Substantial: Samuel J. Eales, Life and Works of Saint Bernard, 4+ vols (Hodges, 1889–96), keyed to the Mabillon/Migne text — free on Internet Archive and the most useful PD set when working directly from PL. CCEL hosts On Loving God, selected letters, Life of St. Malachy. George Lewis, On Consideration (Clarendon, 1908).
modernTranslations: Cistercian Fathers series (Liturgical Press), 23+ volumes 1970–2023: all 86 Sermons on the Song of Songs (Walsh/Edmonds, CF 4/7/31/40); Bruno Scott James's 469 letters (CF 62); On Consideration (CF 37); Steps of Humility and Pride (CF 13); On Grace and Free Choice (CF 19A); complete liturgical-year sermons (CF 51–54); De Diversis (CF 68); Parables & Sentences (CF 55); Marian homilies (CF 18). G.R. Evans, Selected Works (Paulist CWS, 1987). Note: CF series follows the Leclercq–Rochais critical edition, not Migne.
untranslatedHighlights: Minor gaps only: James's letters volume covers 469 of ~547 letters in Leclercq's critical numbering; a few small opuscula unaudited. Best-covered author among the medieval figures in this batch.

name: Bruno Astensis
pdTranslations: No public-domain English translations located.
modernTranslations: No English translations located in Fathers of the Church, ACW, TTH, or other standard medieval translation series.
untranslatedHighlights: Bruno of Asti's biblical commentaries (13 books of Scripture), life of Pope Leo IX, sacramental treatises, Eucharistic theology, and 145 preserved homilies all appear to remain in Latin (PL vols. 164–165). No modern English translation program identified.

name: Anselmus Laudunensis et schola
pdTranslations: No comprehensive public-domain translation located.
modernTranslations: Partial translations: select passages from Anselm of Laon's Commentary on Matthew appear in modern blog/online resources (e.g., 'The Divine Lamp' blog contains translations of specific Gospel passages). No formal, complete English translation of his glossa ordinaria or sentential works located.
untranslatedHighlights: The glossa ordinaria (his principal interlinear Bible commentary, most important scholastic biblical work of early 12th century), full commentaries on Psalms, Song of Songs, Revelation, and Pauline Epistles, plus sentiential collections remain substantially untranslated into English.

name: Hugo de S. Victore
pdTranslations: Essentially none — no ANF/NPNF/Library of the Fathers coverage; earliest significant translations are mid-20th-century and still copyrighted.
modernTranslations: Jerome Taylor, Didascalicon (Columbia, 1961). Roy J. Deferrari, On the Sacraments (De sacramentis, Medieval Academy, 1951; Ex Fontibus reprint 2019). Selected Spiritual Writings (Religious of C.S.M.V., 1962; Wipf & Stock reprint) incl. De arca Noe morali, De vanitate mundi. Victorine Texts in Translation series (Brepols, 10 vols, 2010–2022) — substantial Hugh throughout (VTT 1 Trinity & Creation, VTT 2 On Love, VTT 3/6 Interpretation of Scripture, VTT 10 On the Sacraments), eds. Feiss, Harkins, van Liere, Coolman. Roughly 15-25% of PL corpus translated.
untranslatedHighlights: Adnotationes in Pentateuchon, the 19 Homilies on Ecclesiastes (only selections in VTT), and most shorter exegetical/didactic pieces remain Latin-only (confirmed negative). No FOTC, ACW, or TTH volumes.

name: Auctor incertus (Beda?)
pdTranslations: Cannot determine without specific work identification. If Bedan, follows Bede's translation status.
modernTranslations: Cannot determine without specific work identification.
untranslatedHighlights: This is an uncertain-attribution bucket possibly linked to Bede. Requires identification of constituent pseudo-Bedan works (biblical commentaries, homilies, scientific tracts, etc.) for accurate translation assessment.

name: Alcuinus
pdTranslations: No ANF/NPNF/Library of the Fathers volumes (post-dates their scope). W.S. Howell, The Rhetoric of Alcuin & Charlemagne (Princeton, 1941 — US renewal status varies). Letter excerpts in older compilations (Internet Archive, Fordham sourcebooks).
modernTranslations: Joseph Pucci, The Poetry of Alcuin of York (Routledge, 2023) — first complete translation of the poetic corpus (339 poems). S. Allott, Alcuin of York: His Life and Letters (1974) — selected letters. Peter Godman, Bishops, Kings, and Saints of York (Oxford Medieval Texts, 1983). Song of Songs commentary in Turner, Eros and Allegory (Cistercian CS 156, 1995). Revelation commentary (Van Der Pas, Consolamini, 2016). Ad pueros sancti Martini (Driscoll, Traditio 53, 1998).
untranslatedHighlights: Most biblical commentaries (Genesis Quaestiones, Ecclesiastes, John, Hebrews), De fide sanctae Trinitatis (bilingual CCSL edition exists, no standalone English), grammatical and computistical treatises, and the majority of the 300+ letters. No FOTC or ACW volumes.
